blocks.prompt: 9. Find the equations of the tangent and normal to the parabola \(x^{2} - 6x - 2y + 11 = 0\) at the point \((5, 3)\).
blocks.explanation:
Yeh parabola standard form mein nahi hai (vertex origin par nahi), is liye \(yy_{1} = 2a(x + x_{1})\) wala formula seedha nahi lagega.
Asal tareeqa yaad karein: tangent ki slope = us point par \(\frac{dy}{dx}\).
To di gayi equation ko differentiate karenge, \(x = 5\) rakh kar slope nikalenge, aur point-slope form lagayenge.
Normal ki slope tangent ki slope ka negative reciprocal hogi.
Ek aur raasta bhi hai: complete square se \((x - 3)^{2} = 2(y - 1)\) banta hai, magar differentiate karna yahan sab se seedha hai.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(x^{2} - 6x - 2y + 11 = 0\); point \((5, 3)\).
Maloom karna: \((5, 3)\) par tangent aur normal.
Tareeqa: \(\frac{dy}{dx}\), phir point-slope form.

Point curve par hai?
\[25 - 30 - 6 + 11 = 0\]
Kyun: tangent ka formula sirf curve ke point par lagta hai; pehle tasdeeq kar lena achhi aadat hai.

Tangent ki slope
\[2x - 6 - 2\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 0\]
\[\dfrac{dy}{dx} = x - 3\]
\(x = 5\) par slope \(= 2\).
Kyun: har term ko \(x\) ke lihaz se differentiate kiya: \(x^{2} \to 2x\), \(-6x \to -6\), \(-2y \to -2\frac{dy}{dx}\), constant \(\to 0\).

Tangent
\[y - 3 = 2(x - 5)\]
\[2x - y - 7 = 0\]
Kyun: point-slope form; \(y - 3 = 2x - 10\) ko ek taraf jama kiya.

Normal
Slope \(= -\frac{1}{2}\):
\[y - 3 = -\dfrac{1}{2}(x - 5)\]
\[2y - 6 = -x + 5\]
\[x + 2y - 11 = 0\]
Kyun: \(m_{1}m_{2} = -1\), yaani 2 ka negative reciprocal \(-\frac{1}{2}\); phir 2 se multiply kar ke fraction khatam kiya.
Dhyan dein: sirf ulta karna kaafi nahi, sign bhi badalna hai.

Tasdeeq:
\(y = 2x - 7\) ko curve mein rakhein: \(x^{2} - 6x - 4x + 14 + 11 = x^{2} - 10x + 25 = (x - 5)^{2}\), \(x = 5\) par dohra root: line sirf chhooti hai. \((5, 3)\) normal par bhi hai: \(5 + 6 - 11 = 0\). Answer key bhi yahi deti hai.
